daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo warned regional leaders against enriching themselves at the expense of the public, telling them to avoid getting rich on public suffering and reminding them that thieves have infiltrated the free meal program (MBG). Separately, Prabowo asked police, military, and prosecutors to introspect and ordered regional leaders to oversee the free meal program directly.

  • The Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs backed the police investigation into three corruption cases, stating there is no room for lawbreakers.
  • Chief Prosecutor for Special Crimes (Jampidsus) Febrie Adriansyah resigned from his position after police examined 15 witnesses regarding three alleged corruption cases and a house linked to him was not yet recorded in his wealth report.
  • The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) detained Sukoharjo Regent Etik Suryani in an arrest operation.
  • The Minister of State Apparatus Empowerment and Bureaucratic Reform called for flexible working arrangements for civil servants to accompany their children on the first day of school.
  • The Home Affairs Minister urged local governments to accelerate the housing assistance program targeting 400,000 homes in 2026.
  • Constitutional expert Jimly Asshiddiqie criticized the explanation given by Gerindra Secretary-General Ahmad Muzani about being sent by Prabowo to Iran.
  • The government denied that Presidential Regulation 111 legalizes discrimination against LGBT individuals.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesian Foreign Minister Sugiono arrived in Mashhad, Iran to pay respects to Supreme Leader Khamenei and attend his funeral. President Prabowo refused to sell state defense industries to foreign buyers and revealed he had previously blocked attempts to sell state-owned defense companies abroad.

  • Indonesia and Russia are exploring a maritime technology partnership to modernize Indonesia's maritime industry through technology transfer.
  • Indonesia strengthened its film ecosystem through strategic collaboration with France.
  • The United States returned two bronze statues to Indonesia.
  • Timor Leste arrested 61 Indonesian citizens for online fraud, according to the Foreign Ministry.
  • Prabowo stated that Arab military forces ordered rifles from PT Pindad, saying Indonesian weapons are proven.

Other

President Prabowo inaugurated five dams worth Rp 9.79 trillion and expects them to increase rice production by one million tons. The government also allocated additional coal quotas for PLN to prevent blackouts.

  • Bank Indonesia official Purbaya disclosed plans to place Rp 400 trillion in banks to boost the economy.
  • Investors are eyeing 1.3 GW data center expansion in Indonesia.
  • State holding company Danantara partnered with a U.S. firm to develop coal gasification projects.
  • The Minister of Health reported many complaints of bullying of specialist doctors in Manado and stated that leprosy is not a curse and can be treated.
  • Prabowo issued a presidential instruction for the conservation of Sumatran and Kalimantan elephants.
